blocks.title: <ico-recycle></ico-recycle> REPASO EXPRESS · lección anterior
blocks.intro: Antes de empezar, recupera lo de la clase pasada. Une cada palabra con su significado — sin mirar atrás.

blocks.title: <ico-book></ico-book> MUST / MIGHT / CAN'T + SUAVIZAR
blocks.intro: Dos herramientas para discutir con datos: los modales de deducción (must / might / can't) dicen qué tan seguro estás, y las frases suavizantes te dejan opinar sin sonar agresivo. Cinco pasos. Toca el altavoz de cada línea y repite en voz alta.

vocab.en: to back it up with evidence

vocab.sp: una concesión: ganas algo y pierdes algo

blocks.note: Cómo funciona: tarjetas , comparar , escucha , completar y ordenar . CHECK donde lo veas.

parts.html: 1 · MUST BE — casi seguro que sí

items.en: The server must be overloaded. Look at these numbers.
items.sp: El servidor debe de estar sobrecargado.
Alguien debe de estar trabajando hasta tarde. — ves las luces, sacas la conclusión.

parts.body: Aquí must no es obligación: es una deducción, como «debe de ser» o «seguro que es». La evidencia te lleva a la conclusión.

parts.html: 2 · MIGHT / COULD BE — posible, pero no seguro

items.en: It might be a caching problem.
items.sp: Podría ser un problema de caché.

items.en: The checkout could be loading too slowly.
items.sp: El checkout podría estar cargando demasiado lento.

items.en: She might be in a meeting.

parts.html: 3 · CAN'T BE — casi seguro que no

items.en: It can't be the design. We tested it twice.
He can't be a beginner. His French is perfect.

parts.body: Lo contrario de must be no es mustn't. It mustn't be the design. → It can't be the design. (mustn't = prohibido)

parts.html: 4 · SUAVIZAR TU OPINIÓN — sugerir en vez de ordenar

items.sp: Sugeriría una prueba de una semana.

items.en: It might be worth testing the speed.
items.sp: Podría valer la pena probar la velocidad. — worth + verbo-ing.

items.en: Have you considered a faster option?

parts.body: «You must change it» es una orden. Para sugerir: It might be worth to test it. → It might be worth testing it.

parts.html: 5 · DISCREPAR CON DATOS — reconoces, discrepas, muestras evidencia, propones

items.en: I take your point, but I see it differently.
items.sp: Entiendo tu punto, pero yo lo veo distinto.

items.en: With respect, the data suggests something else.
items.sp: Con todo respeto, los datos sugieren otra cosa.

items.en: Can we look at the evidence together?
If I'm wrong, we go back to the old design. Fair?
items.sp: Ofreces una salida: eso baja la tensión.

blocks.title: <ico-star></ico-star> THE DESIGN DEBATE
blocks.intro: Las ventas de GreenMarket bajaron y Priya cree que el problema es el nuevo diseño de Marcos. Él no está de acuerdo — y tiene datos. ¿Puede defender su trabajo sin quemar la relación?

blocks.title: FRASES SUAVIZANTES · toca para girar
blocks.intro: El mismo mensaje, dicho con tacto. Aprende estas frases — las vas a escuchar en el audio.

blocks.title: MUST BE vs MIGHT BE
blocks.intro: Las dos son deducciones — pero una te compromete casi al 100% y la otra te deja salida. En una discusión con datos, esa diferencia es tu credibilidad.

pair.a: It must be the payment system.
pair.b: It might be the payment system.

items.q: ¿Cuál deja la puerta abierta a otras causas?

options: He might not be a beginner.

items.q: Las luces están encendidas y se oyen voces. ¿Qué dices?

blocks.title: AUDIO 1 · THE DEBATE
blocks.desc: Priya culpa al diseño por la caída de ventas. Marcos discrepa — con datos y con tacto. ¿Quién tiene razón?

questions.q: What does Priya think is the problem?
According to Marcos, what might the real problem be?
options: The new design of the home page

questions.q: How does Marcos know it can't be the design?
options: Sales went up right after the redesign
The old design had the same problem
People stay longer on the new home page

questions.q: What do they agree to do?
options: Go back to the old design on Friday
Run a one-week test on checkout speed

speaking.prompt: How did Marcos push back politely? Quote one softening phrase and one deduction (must/might/can't).
speaking.starter: He said 'I see it differently' and 'it can't be the design, because (his reason)'. Then he suggested (his suggestion).

transcript.html: Marcos, I've seen the numbers. Sales are down fifteen percent since the redesign. It must be the new design. We should go back to the old one.
I take your point, Priya — the timing looks bad. But I see it differently. Can we look at the evidence together?
The data shows people love the new home page — they stay longer than before. But they leave at the checkout page. So it can't be the design. Something else is wrong.
I'm not one hundred percent sure. It might be the new payment system — the checkout could be loading too slowly on phones. Slow pages kill sales.
That's possible. But we can't wait forever.
Agreed. So I'd suggest a one-week test: we measure the checkout speed, and it might be worth trying a faster payment option too. If I'm wrong, we go back to the old design. Fair?
Okay, Marcos. One week. Show me the data next Friday. And… good pushback. I like it when people bring evidence.

blocks.title: MUST, MIGHT o CAN'T
blocks.intro: Elige el modal correcto según la certeza.

items.q: Sales dropped the day we changed servers. It ___ be a coincidence!
The office lights are on and I hear voices. Someone ___ be working late.
I'm not sure why it's slow — it ___ be the wifi.
He answered in perfect French. He ___ be a beginner.
It ___ be worth testing the page on a phone.
She's not answering. She ___ be in a meeting.
It might be worth ___ a faster payment option.
We tested the design twice. It ___ be the problem.

blocks.title: ORDENA LA FRASE DIPLOMÁTICA
blocks.intro: Toca las palabras para formar la sugerencia suave.

items.answer: It might be worth testing the speed
Have you considered a faster option
I take your point but I see it differently

blocks.title: AUDIO 2 · ONE WEEK LATER
blocks.desc: Viernes siguiente: Priya le deja un mensaje a Marcos con el resultado del test. ¿Quién tenía razón?

options: The home page took nine seconds to load
The checkout took nine seconds on phones
The design was driving people away

questions.q: What happened to sales after the fix?
What does Priya thank Marcos for?
When did the team switch to the faster payment option?

speaking.prompt: You are Marcos. Reply to Priya's message in 2–3 sentences — be professional, don't say 'I told you so'!
speaking.starter: Hi Priya, thanks for the update. I'm glad the test helped — I'd suggest we also (next step).

transcript.html: Hi Marcos, it's Priya. It's Friday, so — the results. Well… you were right. It wasn't the design. The test showed the checkout page was taking nine seconds to load on phones. Nine! No wonder people were leaving. The team switched to the faster payment option on Tuesday, and sales have already recovered. So, I owe you one. Thank you for pushing back — and for doing it with data, not drama. That's exactly how I like to work. Enjoy your weekend, Marcos. You've earned it.

blocks.title: <ico-pen></ico-pen> DISAGREE, BUT NICELY
blocks.intro: Tu jefe/a propone algo que te parece un error (elige la situación). Escribe tu respuesta (5–7 frases):
checklist: Reconoce su punto primero (I take your point…)
Marca tu desacuerdo con tacto (I see it differently / With respect,…)
Usa un modal de deducción (must / might / can't be)
Propón un paso siguiente (I'd suggest… / It might be worth…)
blocks.placeholder: Hi …, I take your point about…
blocks.example: I take your point about su idea. However, I see it differently. It can't be causa descartada, because evidencia. It might be causa posible. The data suggests dato. I'd suggest siguiente paso. It might be worth verbo-ing first.
blocks.hw: Escribe tu respuesta y después grábate diciéndola sin leer, con tono calmado y profesional. Envíame texto y audio por WhatsApp.

rubric.d: Escribiste el número de frases que pide la consigna y cubriste todos los puntos.
Usaste el desacuerdo con tacto + must / might / can’t al menos 3 veces, y bien.
Un lector lo entiende sin releer: ideas unidas con conectores, sin traducir literal del español.
